description: HIGH IMPACT: implement the design with tests, in a staging copy; the diff is applied after policy checks

requirements.summary: New project: Spring Boot (Maven) URL shortener with create, redirect, custom alias, click count and validation, tested with JUnit and documented run/test commands.

design.summary: New project: single-module Spring Boot 3.5.6 (Maven, Java) URL shortener with an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap store (putIfAbsent for atomic code/alias uniqueness, AtomicLong click counter), JSON API under /api, root-level GET /{code} 302 redirect, centralized error mapping (422/400/404/409), JUnit 5 + MockMvc tests. | stack: Java (compiled with java.release=17, runs on the locally installed JDK 25)/Spring Boot 3.5.6 (spring-boot-starter-web, spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-test) | test: mvn -B -q test

stack.language: Java (compiled with java.release=17, runs on the locally installed JDK 25)
stack.rationale: Stack is mandated by the requirement (Java, Spring Boot, Maven, JUnit). Boot 3.5.6 parent is already in the local ~/.m2 so build works offline; release 17 is the Boot 3 baseline and compiles on JDK 25. Only three starters to keep supply-chain surface minimal.

api: POST /api/links  body {"url": string, "alias": string optional}  -> 201 {"code", "shortUrl", "url"}; 422 invalid/missing url or invalid/reserved alias; 409 alias taken; 400 unparseable JSON
GET /{code}  -> 302 Found with single Location header = stored URL, Cache-Control: no-store; increments click count by one; 404 unknown code
GET /api/links/{code}  -> 200 {"code", "url", "clicks"}; 404 unknown code; does not change the click count
Error body (all errors): {"error": string, "message": string} with no exception class names or stack traces
shortUrl = app.base-url + "/" + code (never derived from Host / X-Forwarded-Host)
design.rollback_plan: New project with no prior release: rollback is to stop the service and revert/discard the release commit or tag (git revert of the release commit, or redeploy the previous artifact if any). There is no database, schema or migration, and in-memory data is ephemeral, so no data restore is needed; deleting the target/ directory removes build output. If persistence is added later, that release must carry its own forward/backward migration plan.
